subject: Maths
scope: Fifteen Year 1 AQA Pure Maths mock recall cards only. No statistics, mechanics, Year 2 material or radians.
notes: Gives extra recall on proofs, 2D vectors, graph transformations, binomial, sequences, integration and logarithms. Does not replace hard exam questions. Not proof of complete full specification coverage.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: Why is one counterexample enough to disprove a statement claimed to hold for all real numbers?
cards.back: A universal statement is false if even one valid case does not satisfy it.
accept: A universal statement is false if even one valid case does not satisfy it.
One counterexample disproves a claim about every value.
A single allowed failure makes the universal assertion false.
reject: You must check infinitely many values to disprove it.
One confirming example proves a universal claim.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: When can proof by exhaustion establish a statement?
cards.back: When every possible case belongs to a finite list that can all be checked.
accept: When every possible case belongs to a finite list that can all be checked.
Check all cases when there are finitely many possibilities.
It is valid if the set of possible cases is finite and each is verified.
reject: Checking one case is enough even when others differ.
It requires an infinite number of checks.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How can any even integer be represented in a proof by deduction?
accept: As 2k for some integer k.
Write it as twice an integer.
n = 2k where k is an integer.
reject: As k/2 for every real k.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the magnitude of the 2D vector (a,b)?
accept: √(a² + b²).
The square root of a squared plus b squared.
Use Pythagoras, sqrt(a^2+b^2).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: Given position vectors OA = a and OB = b, what is vector AB?
accept: b − a.
Position vector of B minus that of A.
AB = OB − OA.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How can a scalar-multiple argument establish that A, B and C are collinear?
cards.back: Show AB = k AC for some scalar k.
accept: Show AB = k AC for some scalar k.
Prove that AB and AC are parallel by showing one is a multiple of the other.
Demonstrate one displacement vector is a scalar multiple of the other.
reject: Show AB and AC have equal length only.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For a > 1, what transformation maps y = f(x) to y = f(ax)?
cards.back: A horizontal stretch with scale factor 1/a.
accept: A horizontal stretch with scale factor 1/a.
Stretch parallel to the x-axis by factor one over a.
The graph becomes horizontally compressed by factor a.
reject: A vertical stretch of scale factor a.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What transformation maps y = f(x) to y = f(−x)?
accept: Reflection in the y-axis.
Reflect the graph across the y-axis.
Mirror the graph in the vertical axis.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What transformation maps y = f(x) to y = f(x − 4)?
cards.back: Translation four units to the right.
accept: Translation four units to the right.
Move the graph 4 in the positive x-direction.
Shift horizontally right by 4.
reject: Move the graph four units left.
Stretch the graph vertically by four.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a quadratic discriminant of zero tell you about its real roots?
cards.back: There is one repeated real root.
accept: There is one repeated real root.
The quadratic has a repeated real solution.
The two real roots are equal.
reject: There are two distinct real roots.
The quadratic has no real roots.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the r-th term, counting the first term as r = 0, in the expansion of (a + b)^n for positive integer n?
accept: nCr × a^(n−r) × b^r.
The coefficient n choose r times a to n minus r times b to r.
C(n,r) a^(n-r) b^r.
reject: nCr × a^r × b^r for every term.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum of the first n terms of a geometric progression with first term a and ratio r, for r ≠ 1?
accept: a times (1 minus r to the n) over (1 minus r).
reject: Sₙ = a/(1−r) for every finite n.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does the derivative f′(x) represent on the graph y = f(x)?
cards.back: The gradient of the tangent at x.
accept: The gradient of the tangent at x.
Instantaneous rate of change of y with x.
Slope of the tangent to the curve at that point.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: Why may a definite integral not equal the total geometric area between a curve and the x-axis?
cards.back: Regions below the x-axis contribute negative signed area.
accept: Regions below the x-axis contribute negative signed area.
The integral gives signed area, so parts below the axis subtract.
Below-axis contributions are negative rather than positive.
reject: All areas are counted positively automatically.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For positive a and b, what is ln(ab)?
accept: ln a + ln b.
The sum of the two natural logarithms.
Natural log of a product equals log a plus log b.
